caveats: Solar, storage, wind and peak load all rise together across 2011-2026 in ERCOT. The design has one Texas buildout trajectory, not four independent ones, so the individual coefficients on storage_gw / solar_gw / wind_gw are not separately identified: the VIF table is the evidence, and the buildout_index refit is the same data with the collinearity acknowledged.

prm_summer is a single column spanning four documented ERCOT methodology breaks (Dec 2014 wind ELCC, Dec 2019 NPRR958/959, May 2022 parallel PRM series, Dec 2024 true-ELCC with batteries; see the header of curated/reserve_margin.csv). Its coefficient is a summary of a discontinuous series, not a structural elasticity.

Every projection year is outside the fitted covariate support -- 2029 base has storage at 38.5 GW against a fitted maximum of 17.9 GW, and the high scenarios put peak load 60+ GW above anything observed. An exponential-mean count model extrapolates multiplicatively, so those rows are flagged 'extrapolated' and are reported next to hours_support_capped (the same model evaluated only where it has seen data). Where the two differ by orders of magnitude, neither is a forecast; the scenario fan is the honest object.

No weather parquet exists in this repo yet, so temp_anom_c and its square are dropped from the design. Month fixed effects absorb the average seasonal shape but not the year-to-year weather that actually causes scarcity -- part of what the era dummies are picking up is hot summers.
Standard errors treat the NB dispersion alpha as known at its profile-likelihood maximum, the usual GLM convention; they are mildly optimistic.
current_regime.csv is model-free: a rate and an NB-dispersion interval over 2024-01 to the end of the panel. It carries none of the above caveats and is the number the site should headline.
